title: Shooter buttons in OI
summary: A button is just true or false: write getShootButton() and getIndexButton().

steps.title: A button is true or false

say.never: A button can only be two things: held (**true**) or not held (**false**). A method that answers a yes/no question is written with `boolean`. For example a door sensor can answer "is the door open?" with `true` or `false`. A controller button answers the same kind of question.
say.bit: A yes/no question is a `boolean`: true or false, like a door sensor or a button.

marks.label: true or false, nothing in between

say.never: The buttons live in the same class as the sticks. Hold down **Ctrl** and tap **P**. A small search box pops up at the top. Type `OI`, then press **Enter**. It finds any file by its name, so you never have to dig through folders.
say.bit: The buttons live in the same class as the sticks. Press **Ctrl+P**, type `OI` and press Enter. Quick Open finds any file by name, so you never have to dig through folders.

say.never: The first one is the shoot button. Click in the code, then hold **Ctrl** and tap **F** to open the search box. Type `right bumper is held` and press **Enter**. The editor scrolls to the right spot and highlights it.
say.bit: The first one is the shoot button. Press **Ctrl+F**, type `right bumper is held` and press Enter to jump to it.

target.text: return true while the right bumper is held

waitFor.hint: find right bumper is held with Ctrl+F.

say.never: Find the line that says `return false;` right under that comment. Change it to `return driverController.getRightBumperButton();`. Now this method returns true while the right bumper is held.

target.text: return true while the right bumper is held
